(2) The escape prefix is visible in output geometry: every non-Sans width path counts U+10F7FF as a glyph. findings: HELD-OUT FAILURE, packet mechanism (width rule): BE pua_b_upper_escape_point, source class "%upper("a U+10F7FF b U+10FFFF")", DIFF 5. Java textLength is 38.7119 and the tip's is 42.2119 (+3.5 = 14 - 10.5). U+10FFFF is outside is_supplementary_private_use, so it falls to the 1 em fallback; Java uses 0.75 em. Not a regression (base DIFF; round 3 crashes).

Width provenance: Java's SansSerif on the reference Mac is Lucida Grande (fonttrace.py: its hmtx matches all 95 CHAR_WIDTHS_14 ASCII advances exactly). Its .notdef advance is 1536/2048 = 0.75 em, in regular and bold, and the font maps none of U+10FFFD, U+10FFFF or U+F0000. So the constant has a real mechanism: Java's missing-glyph advance for code points the font chain cannot map. The draft cites only five BC measurements and limits the rule to planes-15/16 private use, a scope BE falsifies. Rule 1 requires the named mechanism, and the scope must follow it. This is an environment font fact recorded as a diagnostic, not a new renderer constant.

ESCAPE VISIBLE IN OUTPUT (new defect, base->tip, Rust-only; Java references staged): family_text_width (crates/rustuml-render/src/text_render.rs:1382) measures raw chars for Mono, CourierNew, Arial, Helvetica, Verdana and TimesNewRoman. Only plantuml_metrics::text_width (Sans) is token-aware, so U+10F7FF counts as a glyph. 'Vault U+10FFFD' textLength: Arial 49.7998 -> 60.2998 (+10.5), Courier and Monospaced 59.001 -> 67.4297 (+8.4287, one cell), Times New Roman 45.4932 -> 56.3828 (+10.8896). The same happens for U+10FFFF under Arial. Java cannot measure a character that is not in its string.

COLLISION (new valid-input errors base->tip, Rust-only; Java references staged as cr_json_u_escape and cr_yaml_u_escape): @startyaml 'k: "Vault \U0010FFFD end"' and @startjson '{"k": "Vault \uDBFF\uDFFD end"}' exit 1 with 'export error: An invalid XML character (Unicode: 0xdffd)', and --ast/--yaml show U+FFFD, where base renders U+10FFFD. Cause: parse_yaml/parse_json/parse_auto_with_base escape the raw text, but serde then decodes an escape sequence into an unescaped reserved scalar that java_utf16::tokens reads as a carrier. The JSON case is declared residue; the YAML double-quoted escape is not. A valid surrogate-pair escape is ordinary text in Java, and both are new valid-input errors.

Entry points examined without a defect (Rust-only probes, exit and visibility vs base): %chr(1114109) (goes through Value::from_utf16, escaped); creole 􏿽, 􏿽 and <U+10FFFD> (passed through, no raw reserved scalar); ~ before U+10FFFD; sprites, !define, !procedure, TIM JSON variables, stereotypes, URL/tooltip attributes, multi-line notes, mindmap, maxMessageSize wrapping across 10 PUA-B scalars; PUA-B entity codes (ids). stdin and file input both go through PreprocessContext::process. Not applicable or not exercised: -D (the CLI has no -D), %filename (returns empty, pre-existing), %load_json (registered, not implemented), !includeurl (no network in the checker), --theme-file YAML (not escaped; style values). salt with PUA-B panics in base and tip alike (pre-existing).
